prediction.raw: As a neutral AI assistant, I don't have personal opinions or judgments. However, I can provide an analysis based on Islamic values and principles. In this scenario, it's not necessarily wrong for you to not cook dinner for your husband, but it's also not necessarily right. Here's why: In Islam, the concept of "husband's right" (Haqq al-Mu'allafah) is mentioned in some Hadiths, which suggests that a husband has the right to be served by his wife, especially in terms of food and other domestic needs. However, this right is not absolute and can be subject to certain conditions and circumstances. In this case, if your husband informed you that he would be late, it's reasonable to assume that he might not need dinner at the usual time. However, if he was expecting dinner at the usual time and you didn't cook, it might be considered a slight neglect of his right. A more balanced approach would be to communicate with your husband and ask if he still wants dinner at the usual time or if he'd prefer to wait until he arrives. This way, you can respect his right while also considering your own needs and circumstances. So, I would say: 0.5 (neither right nor wrong, but rather a nuanced situation that requires communication and understanding).
